In addition to the witness identifying the male and female on the bike, body cam footage of the moment the officer was run over by the motorcycle shows the same green shirt the male was wearing, the same black shorts, the same muscular build, as well as the same purple pants the injured female was wearing, confirming these were indeed the same people. The male suspect was identified as Armando Fogaza, a Floridian fitness influencer and bodybuilder born in Brazil. He's gained well over 700,000 followers on Instagram from videos he's posted of himself accomplishing large feats of strength, like crushing a watermelon with his bare hands, poking a hole in a Coke can, bending a hammer, and more. In one of his posts he can actually be seen wearing the exact outfit with the green shirt and black shorts he had in the body cam footage. Armando's wife, who was the female passenger with him, is also featured on his Instagram account. She was transported to a nearby hospital's trauma center and treated for her injuries. The officer who was run over by Armando was also transported to the hospital to be treated for fractured ribs, abrasions, and bruising throughout his entire body. After fleeing from the officer, Armando's wife later revealed to police that they were traveling between 80 and 100 miles an hour before they crashed into a vehicle, throwing her off the motorcycle. Police have stated that Armando also has no driver's license, only a Brazilian passport. Armando was charged with leaving the scene of a crash causing serious bodily injury, driving without a valid license causing serious injury, fleeing and eluding a law enforcement officer, reckless driving, causing serious bodily injury, and aggravated battery on a law enforcement officer, totaling five felonies. He is also facing an immigration hold due to his charges. He is currently being held in the Turner-Gilford Knight Correctional Center with no bond. Court records indicate his trial is set for January 5, 2006. While he hasn't yet been sentenced, depending on plea deals and concurrent versus consecutive sentencing, Armando could face up to 20 to 60 plus years in prison for his five felonies. He is innocent unless proven guilty in a court of law. There's a certain kind of danger that never announces itself with gunfire or screaming because in this case it's just a guy on a motorcycle. One moment an officer is stepping out into the roadway just to do his job, trusting the public to act like adults. And in a split second, that trust gets shattered by someone who has zero respect for the uniform. When this guy hit the officer, this was a decision made out of fear and ego, and he probably thought that running would keep him safe, like speed was going to erase the consequences waiting behind him. People rarely understand the weight of the split second for the officer. The moment we're stepping out to enforce traffic isn't just procedure, but it's like a silent contract that the public will respect the badge. But there's a certain percentage of people that simply won't. This clip reminds me how thin control really is, how every stop is a risk, where the officers exposed, vulnerable and standing on faith that the person in front of them will not choose anarchy. And police see these patterns over and over, people who treat a lawful stop like a personal insult like the officers ruining their day instead of preventing a tragedy. And these decisions on the road sadly in lives every day. And we have to keep in mind, society only works when people accept limits. Speed, limits, stop signs, red lights. Those aren't inconveniences. Their guard rails meant to keep people alive. When you ignore them and play with people's lives, you aren't rebelling. There are many you can't coexist without risk someone else's future.
